themes_detail.label: Street Vendor Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor Enforcement complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK compared to a baseline average of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 2300% increase with z-score of 8.69—suggesting either a sudden enforcement crackdown or emerging vendor conflict in Coney Island/Brighton Beach.
evidence: 3 vendor enforcement complaints this week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.69)
Statistically significant spike indicates sudden change rather than noise
Timing coincides with boardwalk/beach season in Coney Island
reporting_angles: Is NYPD or Parks enforcement conducting new operations against street vendors on the boardwalk or beach?
Are vendors reporting harassment or are residents complaining about vendor activity?

themes_detail.label: Lot Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Lot Condition complaints reached 3 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 1100% spike with z-score of 4.16—indicating emerging blight or abandonment issues in residential or commercial lots.
evidence: 3 lot condition complaints this week vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.16)
Aligns with 220 active DOB permits (162 alterations, 30 new buildings) that may be leaving sites unsecured or unmaintained
Suggests potential connection to construction activity or property neglect
reporting_angles: Are vacant lots connected to the active ULURP projects (Coney Development, West 24th Street rezoning)?
Are property owners leaving sites unsecured after construction halts or permit approval?

themes_detail.label: Animal in Park Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Animal in a Park complaints jumped to 10 LAST WEEK from a baseline average of 1.4 per week—a 627% spike with z-score of 7.76—suggesting either wildlife encroachment or dangerous animal incidents in Coney Island parks.
evidence: 10 animal-in-park complaints last week vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.76)
Correlates with 7 Dead Animal complaints 2 weeks ago (522% spike, z-score: 7.53)
Pattern suggests both living animal incursions and carcass cleanup failures
reporting_angles: What species are residents encountering in Coney Island parks—rats, coyotes, seals, or other wildlife?
Is Parks Department responding to dead animal removals; what are response times?
Are baiting or population control measures being considered?

themes_detail.label: Street Maintenance and Cleanliness Breakdown
themes_detail.summary: Street Sweeping Complaints and Street Sign Missing complaints both surged last week (7 and 4 respectively versus baselines of 1.0 and 0.4 per week)—600% and 967% increases with z-scores of 6.0 and 5.21—indicating systemic street maintenance gaps.
evidence: 7 street sweeping complaints last week vs. 1.0 weekly average (z-score: 6.0)
4 missing street signs last week vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.21)
Suggests either budget cuts, staffing shortages, or deferred maintenance in sanitation and DOT operations
reporting_angles: Has DSNY reduced street sweeping schedules or coverage in CD 313?
Are street signs being removed as part of construction projects without replacement?
Is there a pattern of requests to elected officials about street cleanliness?

themes_detail.label: Vehicle Noise and Enforcement Issues
themes_detail.summary: Noise - Vehicle complaints spiked to 6 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 1.1 per week—a 433% increase with z-score of 5.26—while Real Time Enforcement complaints also surged to 5 the same period, suggesting either illegal street racing/vehicle activity or failed enforcement response.
evidence: 6 vehicle noise complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.1 weekly average (z-score: 5.26)
5 real time enforcement complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average (z-score: 6.29)
Correlation suggests residents perceiving both noise violations and inadequate NYPD response
reporting_angles: Are illegal street racing or car meets occurring on Coney Island boardwalk or neighborhood streets?
What is NYPD's response time and enforcement rate for noise complaints in the district?
Are residents using Real Time Enforcement app due to perception of slow police response?
